description: The MCP tools POST /mcp serves, as tools/list answers them, sorted by name.

tools.description: Act in a project's ecosystem channel under the credential's own role: a viewer reads, a member writes. Reads: register, inbox, outbox, unanswered (what this side owes a reply to: the work a master takes), read (one document), thread, contracts (a project API page). Writes: draft, reply (a draft answering a number), edit, submit (publishes, or waits at the approve gate), hold and release a conversation, withdraw, supersede, gate (approve or return a document waiting at the approve gate; an admin decides). The author is stamped from the credential and never read from the arguments: in chat the person, via assistant; on /mcp an agent token writes via master and a personal one via cli. Show a person a draft and submit it only once they confirm; hold, withdraw and supersede need a reason. You read only documents this project sends or receives, never another pair or a counterparty internal; in a chat at ecosystem scope you also read those of the person's other projects in that ecosystem, and you still write only as this project. A refusal comes back as { code, path, detail }; say what was refused and why.

by.description: supersede: the number of the published replacement.

decision.description: gate: approve, or return to the writer.

dueBy.description: YYYY-MM-DD; a default applies when omitted.

ecosystem.description: Ecosystem uuid; omit when this project is in one.

note.description: gate: what to change; a return needs one.

project.description: contracts: the project whose API page to read.

projectId.description: The side to act for; a token bound to one project, or the X-Forge-Project-Slug header, names it when omitted.

ref.description: A document uuid, or its number such as FP-CN-3.

thread.description: The number of the document that opened the conversation.

tools.name: forge_channel

tools.description:
What the product is designed as, and the decisions on it: workflow designs, suggestions and mockups. Reading is open to anyone on the project; a decision (approve, return, accept, reject) is the act of whoever holds its permission — workflow-designs.approve, suggestions.approve, mockups — and the service refuses anyone else by name. Decide only what the person asked you to.
Workflow designs:
- design_list { projectId, view? }: every workflow with its design status, revision, approved revision and health.
- design_get { projectId, workflowId, view?: summary | steps | full, revision?, stepFrom?, stepTo? }: one design, whom it waits on, and `progress`: each issue building it, whether an agent works on it now, and when it is likely done.
- design_create { projectId, body: { baseRevision: null, document } } and design_revise { projectId, workflowId, body: { baseRevision, document, issue? } }: write a workflow document (the revision you read is the base).
- design_propose { projectId, workflowId, revision, issue? }: propose a revision for approval.
- design_decide { projectId, workflowId, revision, decision: approve | return, reason? }: a return says why.
- design_withdraw { projectId, workflowId, reason? }: take back a design no revision of which was approved; it leaves the list and Needs you. An approved design is refused DESIGN_WITHDRAW_APPROVED, one another live design names in basedOn DESIGN_WITHDRAW_PINNED.
Suggestions (on a requirement, issue, feedback item or workflow):
- suggestion_list { projectId, requirement? | issue? | feedback? | workflow?, status?: [proposed, accepted, rejected, stale, withdrawn], view? }: summaries; view full reads each payload, a breakdown's slices among them.
- suggestion_create { projectId, body: { kind: requirement_draft | revision_diff | readiness | breakdown | triage | duplicate | feedback_triage | design_change, requirement | issue | feedback | workflow, baseRevision: number | null, payload, model?, rationale?, supersedes? } — baseRevision is the target's revision you read (a revision_diff on a requirement with an open revision takes that open one), or null where there is none: an issue, a feedback item, a requirement with no current revision; rationale (at most 4000 characters) and supersedes (an earlier suggestion's id in this project) stay on the suggestion and are never copied into what its accept writes }.
- suggestion_accept { projectId, suggestionId, reason? }: accepting writes what it suggests. Accepting a breakdown files its issues at draft: that is how a requirement becomes delivery work, so read every slice before you accept.
- suggestion_reject { projectId, suggestionId, reason }, suggestion_revise { projectId, suggestionId, payload, reason } (rejects the original, proposes yours), suggestion_withdraw { projectId, suggestionId } (its producer only).
Mockups (MK-n): a screen or call proposed on the requirement, feedback item or issue it shapes, for a person to try, comment on and accept or return; never a local file. Method: GET /api/guides/mockups.md.
- mockup_list { projectId, requirement | feedback | issue }, mockup_get { projectId, mockup }, mockup_comments { projectId, mockup }: every comment on it and its earlier revisions, with where each points.
- mockup_propose { projectId, body: { target: { requirement, revision? } | { feedback } | { issue } (optional with revises), kind: wireframe | sketch | image | html | api_example, caption?, exactly one of { name, mime?, contentBase64 }, { document } (a wireframe-v1 board) or { source: { from: issue | comment, attachmentId }, name? }, revises?: MK-n (a returned mockup this is the next revision of), answers?: [{ comment, note? }], resolves?: [{ comment, note }] } }. An HTML page is one self-contained file (inline CSS, scripts, data: images; only Google Fonts and cdnjs, jsdelivr or unpkg libraries load): it runs sandboxed and calls nothing. A returned one is answered by proposing it again with revises, settling each comment you addressed.
- mockup_comment { projectId, mockup, body: { body, pin?: { x, y } (a point) | { x, y, w, h } (a region), each a fraction 0..1 of the frame } }.
- mockup_accept { projectId, mockup, reason? } (an accepted requirement mockup is pinned by the next agree or re-pin), mockup_return { projectId, mockup, reason }, mockup_withdraw { projectId, mockup }.

body.description: design_create/_revise, suggestion_create, mockup_propose, mockup_comment: the REST body

feedback.description: a feedback item key (FB-n) or uuid

view.description: design_list: summary | full; design_get: summary | steps | full

workflowId.description: design_*: the workflow whose design this is

tools.name: forge_design

tools.description: Read and write a project's ecosystem records: its interface, the links its own code holds to the contracts it consumes, its builder runs, and an ecosystem's bus. Reads: interface, links, link, builder_runs, builder_run, context (the contracts a run touching { paths } calls: per link with a call site under a path, its guide notes and the measured diff from its pinned version to the latest; recorded on { session } when named), bus (an ecosystem as this token may see it; each link carries impact: whether the latest version of its contract version passes or breaks it, naming the fields, call sites and outside-contract surface it breaks). Writes take { baseRevision, document } as their REST route does: interface_write (a holder of contracts.write; changing commitment windows that are already set also takes commitments.write, which a full token holds where its holder does and a named token only where its grant names it, PERMISSION_FORBIDDEN otherwise), link_create and link_update (link-v1, only by the consuming project's own agent; a link's pinnedVersion and a consumption's builtAgainst name an approved version, CONTRACT_VERSION_NOT_APPROVED for a proposed or returned one), builder_run_create and builder_run_update (builder-run-v1; a join or a push opens the run itself, so a master updates the open one, and a finished run's answer carries report.declaredWithoutCallSite), builder_run_supersede ({ run, reason }: closes an open run as superseded and opens a fresh manual run with the steps the project's current source type derives, waking its master; the project's own agent's, or an org admin's of the steward or the project's org). contract_version_publish ({ contract, version, kind, source, sourceRef }, POST /api/projects/:id/contracts/:contract/versions on REST) records a version of a contract this project publishes with artifact { upload: true }: kind is graphql (SDL text), mcp-tools ({ tools: [{ name, inputSchema }] }), openapi or json-schema, and must be the publication's type; core indexes its elements and measures it against the latest version. Refused by name: CONTRACT_KIND_UNKNOWN, CONTRACT_KIND_MISMATCH, ARTIFACT_UNREADABLE (an openapi artifact the pinned oasdiff cannot load among them), VERSION_BUMP_TOO_SMALL, VERSION_NOT_IN_SCHEME, VERSION_NOT_MEASURED (semver, a change no differ measured: name the version), VERSION_CHANGE_UNKNOWN (semver, a change measured unknown: name the version; it is recorded unknown, never forced to a MAJOR), CONTRACT_NOT_PUBLISHED, PERMISSION_FORBIDDEN (the writer rule of interface_write). contract_version_decide ({ contract, version, decision: approve | return, reason? }, POST /api/projects/:id/contracts/:contract/versions/:version/decision on REST) decides a proposed version: a recorded version is proposed, and current only once approved. Whoever holds contracts.approve (project admin, or an org owner or admin), person or agent alike decides any version, breaking included. Refused by name: PERMISSION_FORBIDDEN, CONTRACT_VERSION_NOT_PROPOSED, CONTRACT_DECISION_REASON_MISSING. The writer is the token, never a field of the document. A refusal comes back as { code, path, detail } under the service's own code, nothing written. For the channel, use forge_channel.

baseRevision.description: A write: the revision this was read at, or null for a first write.

contract.description: contract_version_publish, contract_version_decide: the publication slug of a contract this project publishes.

kind.description: contract_version_publish: graphql, mcp-tools, openapi or json-schema; the publication type.

paths.description: context: repository-relative paths the run touches.

projectId.description: The project acted for; a token bound to one project, or the X-Forge-Project-Slug header, names it when omitted.

reason.description: builder_run_supersede: why the open run is replaced, 1 to 1000 characters. contract_version_decide: why, required to return.

run.description: builder_run, builder_run_update, builder_run_supersede: the builder run uuid.

session.description: context: the agent session uuid to record what was loaded on.

source.description: contract_version_publish: the artifact, SDL text for graphql, the { tools } JSON for mcp-tools.

sourceRef.description: contract_version_publish: where the artifact was read, <repository path>@<commit sha>.

version.description: contract_version_publish: the version name, in the interface versioning scheme, after the latest.

tools.name: forge_ecosystem

tools.description: Feedback about Forge itself — its CLI, routes, MCP tools, guides, web app or pipeline — from any project you work in. It is filed into Forge’s own home project as you (your own account, person or agent), whether or not you are a member there; it never writes into the project you work in. A project’s own feedback is project_feedback. submit { kind: bug | change_request | question | idea | contract_change, title, target: { kind: page | command | route | tool | guide | skill | other, ref }, body?, severity?: low | medium | high | critical, signalKey?, clientVersion?, from?: { project?, issue?, run? } (uuids), writtenLang?: en | vi }: file it. A box credential’s live session names the project, issue and run it came from (its job’s, or its declared run’s); from names them otherwise. A report whose signalKey (absent: its kind and title) an open item already holds is added to that item as an occurrence, never filed twice — the answer says created:false. list: the items you reported, each with phase, origin and `progress` (whether work runs, who it waits on, and the forecast or why there is none; repeat `progress.says`, never a date it does not hold). get {feedback}: one item you reported (a member of the home project reads any), with `shipEvidence` once its work shipped: the violated criterion’s verdict on the running build and its clip. progress {feedback}: its progress block alone. verify {feedback, evidence} and reopen {feedback, evidence}: once its work shipped (phase resolved) and its progress waits on you, confirm the fix or reopen the item, as its reporter. evidence is what you ran against the shipped build and what you saw; an agent is refused FEEDBACK_EVIDENCE_REQUIRED without it, and FORGE_FEEDBACK_NOT_YOURS on an item another account filed. FORGE_HOME_NOT_SET: this instance names no home project, and nothing was written. A refusal answers { error: { code, message, refusals: [{ code, path, detail }] } } and writes nothing.

evidence.description: verify, reopen: what you ran against the shipped build and what you saw; an agent always sends it

feedback.description: get, progress, verify, reopen: the item, FB-n

target.description: submit: the ONE place in Forge it was met — { kind: command, ref: "forge claim --next" }; kind is page (a web address), command, route (METHOD /path), tool (an MCP tool), guide, skill or other

tools.name: forge_feedback

tools.description:
Delivery work as a person following it reads it: each issue's status, whether an agent is working on it now, and when it is likely done (the forecast's dates, or plainly why there is none). It reads; it files nothing.
- action=list { projectId, status?, statusNot?, search?, limit?, offset? }: issues most recently changed first, each with key, title, status, priority and `progress`. `pause` names a wait that holds the whole project, such as no runner online.
- action=get { projectId, issue }: one issue with its description, the questions it waits on, and `progress`.
- action=create: refused (MCP_FILES_FEEDBACK_NOT_ISSUES). An MCP client files no issue. Issues are the delivery side: Forge files one only when a requirement's breakdown is accepted, or when feedback is triaged as delivery work, so the product record always leads. Record what the person means instead, after they confirm it: (1) a problem, bug, change or idea someone reported is Feedback (project_feedback; kind bug | change_request | idea | question), linked to the requirement it touches, and its triage files the issue; (2) new or changed behaviour is a Requirement or a revision of one (forge_requirements), and accepting its breakdown (forge_design suggestion_accept) files the issues, so read every slice first; (3) a question about work already under way is forge_questions ask on that issue. When to step in: ask the person before recording anything, and never accept a breakdown or a triage on your own: each files delivery work, so the person decides it. Work so urgent it fits none of these is filed by the person in the Forge web app, not from here.

issue.description: get: an issue key (ISS-12) or uuid

tools.name: forge_issues

tools.description:
Questions waiting on a person, the person's answer to one, and a person's own question on an issue.
- action=list { projectId, status?: open | answered | void | expired | needs_info (open by default), issue?, limit?, cursor? }: what is owed an answer, newest first, each with its prompt, its options (locked where you may not choose one) and the recommended one. `issue` narrows to one issue's questions. Read `hasMore` and pass `nextCursor` back as `cursor` for the next page.
- action=get { projectId, questionId }: one question with every round, and `progress`: the issue it parks, whether work on it is running, and when it is likely done once answered.
- action=answer { projectId, questionId, round, optionId | text, note?, stillWaits? }: { round, optionId | text, note?, stillWaits? }: round is the round being answered, as an integer, and the answer is exactly one of optionId (one of the question's options) or text (a free answer). Answer only with what the person told you in this conversation, in their words; never answer on your own reading of the question, its recommendation or the code, and when they have not said, ask them. The answer is theirs, recorded with this token and this client: it answers a question a person owes, within what they could answer signed in, and is refused PERMISSION_FORBIDDEN naming the permission an option takes that they do not hold. A question blocked on another agent is that agent's to answer: QUESTION_BLOCKED_ON_AGENT. QUESTION_NOT_OPEN: it is already answered. QUESTION_ROUND_STALE: get it again and show them the new round.
- action=ask { projectId, issue, body, parentId? }: raise your own question on an issue, as a question comment the agent working it owes a reply. To question a requirement or report a problem, use Feedback or the requirement instead: an issue is delivery work, and a question there is about that work.

body.description: ask: your question, as the person would write it

cursor.description: list: the nextCursor of the last page

issue.description: an issue key (ISS-12) or uuid: list its questions, or ask on it

parentId.description: ask: the comment it replies to, if any

tools.name: forge_questions

tools.description:
A project's releases: what shipped, what is drafted, what waits on approval, and the acts a person takes on one. Every answer about a release still moving carries `progress`: whether work is running now, and when it is likely done (the forecast's dates), or plainly why there is no date.
- action=list { projectId, state?, limit? }: releases newest first, each with version, state (draft | in_progress | awaiting_approval | returned | shipped | failed | aborted), name, summary, releasedAt, issue count, requirements, what was verified, and whom it waits on. `draft` is the release now gathering issues: how many are still to land, which an agent is working on, and when it is likely in people's hands.
- action=get { projectId, version }: one release in full: what users get (notes by section), the requirements it completes, its issues with their proof, what stands in the way, the approval, every attempt at it.
- action=page { projectId, version, view? }: the release page a reader reads (user view, or developer for the technical notes).
- action=name { projectId, version, name, summary }: name a drafted or cut release. Needs project admin, as cutting does.
- action=decide { projectId, version, decision: approve | return, reason? }: decide the approval request the release run is waiting on. This is a person's act: it needs releases.approve on the project, and an approval is judged by the release approval checklist (refused CHECKLIST_INCOMPLETE naming the gap). A return must say why. Read the release (get) before you decide, and decide only when the person asked you to.

name.description: name: the release name, a few words

reason.description: decide: why; a return must say why

state.description: list: only releases in this state

summary.description: name: two or three sentences on what it brings

tools.name: forge_releases

tools.description: A project's requirements (REQ-n), for a BA: read them, draft and revise them, and tell the person how delivery is going. Every list row and get answer carries `progress`: `running` (a run works on it right now), `runs` (unfinished runs on its issues: issue, state, step), `waitingOn` (who owes what before it goes on: an agree, a breakdown, a release act; `late` when overdue), `work` (its issues: total, shipped, awaitingRelease, toDo) and `eta` — {estimate:true, likelyBy (p50), almostSurelyBy (p85), of: hands|landing, basis, confidence} read off the project’s own history, or {estimate:false, done, why} saying why no date can be given. `progress.says` is the block in one paragraph: tell it to the person, and never give a date the block does not hold. Actions. list {state?}: every requirement with its state, whom it waits on, criteria proven of total, and progress. get {requirement}: one in full — its latest revision (spec, criteria with codes), revisions, questions standing on it, issues, releases, linked feedback, progress. NOT_FOUND when the project holds no such key. progress {requirement}: the progress block alone. similar {text}: the requirements nearest a wish; call it before create, and revise the one that covers it instead. provider_not_configured or withheld_by_policy does not mean none is similar. create {title, criteria?, reason?, spec?, tldr?, kind?, picture?, designs?, writtenLang?}: a NEW draft requirement at revision 1, as POST /api/projects/:id/requirements writes it; with no reason its author is asked why. REQUIREMENT_DESIGN_UNKNOWN names a design the project lacks. revise {requirement, baseRevision, criteria, reason?, spec?, tldr?, changeSummary?, kind?, picture?}: a new draft revision on the head — use it to change an agreed requirement. Write the WHOLE criteria list: each criterion that stays keeps its code, a new one has none. REQUIREMENT_REVISION_OPEN: a draft or proposed revision is open, so pass revision: n to rewrite that draft instead. REQUIREMENT_REVISION_STALE: the head moved, get it again. propose {requirement, revision}: put a draft revision before the people who agree it. answer {requirement, questionId, round, optionId | answer}: answer a question standing on the requirement (one get lists under questions), as POST /api/questions/:id/answer does — { round, optionId | text, note?, stillWaits? }: round is the round being answered, as an integer, and the answer is exactly one of optionId (one of the question's options) or text (a free answer), the free answer passed here as answer. Answer only with what the person told you in this conversation, in their words; never answer on your own reading of the question, the spec or the code, and when they have not said, ask them. The answer is theirs, recorded with this token and this client: it answers a question a person owes, within what they could answer signed in; one blocked on another agent is refused QUESTION_BLOCKED_ON_AGENT. QUESTION_NOT_OPEN: it is already answered. Agreeing, accepting, returning, deferring and dropping are a person’s sign-off on the requirement page; this tool does none of them. A refusal answers { error: { code, message, refusals: [{ code, path, detail }] } } and writes nothing: tell the person the detail.

answer.description: answer: the person’s words, on a free-text round

baseRevision.description: revise: the head you read (currentRevision from get), null where it has none

criteria.description: revise: the whole list, each criterion that stays with its code

designs.description: create: the workflow designs it relates to, by flow name or id; each is linked

optionId.description: answer: the option the person chose

projectId.description: the project; left out, the X-Forge-Project-Slug header or the token’s one project

questionId.description: answer: a question standing on the requirement

revision.description: revise: the draft revision to rewrite whole; propose: the draft revision to propose

state.description: list: keep only requirements in this state

title.description: create: the requirement’s title, in the person’s words

tools.name: forge_requirements

tools.description: READ an issue, comment or session attachment so you can analyze it: the one Forge read no shell command can do, because an image comes back as a viewable image block. Uploading is `POST /api/issues/:id/attachments` (multipart) or `forge attach`. data={target:"issue"|"comment"|"session", attachmentId:<uuid from any attachments[].id>}. Images (png/jpeg/gif/webp) return as a viewable image block; the structured answer carries no bytes, so it says `inlined: false` with `reason: image_block_in_content` and names the block as `image: { contentIndex, mimeType }`. Text/markdown return inline, framed as data, with `inlined: true`. PDFs/video and oversized files (> inline cap) return metadata only. EVERY fetch also returns `downloadUrl` (+ `downloadExpiresAt`): a short-lived, self-authenticating URL to `curl` the raw bytes onto disk or hand to a service that must fetch the file itself. Treat it as a secret: do not log it or paste it into a comment.
tools.name: forge_uploads

tools.description: A project's own feedback (FB-n) — what people report or wish about that project's product — for a BA: read it, file it, ask its reporter, and tell them how the work it became is going. Feedback about Forge itself is forge_feedback. Every list row and get answer carries `progress` for the work the item was routed to (its issues, or the requirement it became; a duplicate reads its root’s): `running` (a run works on it right now), `runs` (unfinished runs: issue, state, step), `waitingOn` (who owes what: a triage, a release act, an answer), `work` (issues total, shipped, awaitingRelease, toDo) and `eta` — {estimate:true, likelyBy (p50), almostSurelyBy (p85), of: hands|landing, basis, confidence}, or {estimate:false, done, why} saying why no date can be given (not triaged yet, declined, answered, routed to a revision, no issue yet). `progress.says` is the block in one paragraph: tell it to the person, and never give a date the block does not hold. Actions. list {phase?: [new|triaged|planned|resolved|reopened|verified|declined], q?, requirement? (REQ-n)}: the items with phase, route, whom each waits on, and progress. get {feedback}: one in full — body, where seen, route and carriers, decisions, the open clarification and its answer, progress. NOT_FOUND when the project holds no such key. progress {feedback}: the progress block alone. similar {feedback}: the items nearest it, to spot a duplicate; not_embedded, provider_not_configured, failed or withheld_by_policy does not mean none is similar. submit { kind: bug | change_request | question | idea | contract_change, title, body?, severity?: low | medium | high | critical, whereSeen?, exactly one of requirement | issue | release | workflow | endpoint | mockup | screen, node?: { step } | { edge: { from, to, label? } } (with workflow only), writtenLang?: en | vi }: file it as the person you speak for, at phase new. Name exactly one target; a requirement it touches is best (find it with forge_requirements). clarify {feedback, prompt, needed, recommended}: ask the reporter one question; `needed` says what would settle it, `recommended` is the answer you recommend, which they send by one click. Refused while one is open on the item or to the same reporter, or when the item is past triage. Triage, decline, verify and retarget are a person’s acts on the Feedback page; this tool does none of them. Issues are never filed from here: triage routes an item to its work. A refusal answers { error: { code, message, refusals: [{ code, path, detail }] } } and writes nothing: tell the person the detail.

projectId.description: the project; left out, the X-Forge-Project-Slug header or the token’s one project

tools.name: project_feedback
